title: What are Models?
description: Understand the role of models in Django – they are your database tables represented as Python classes.

slides.title: Models: The Bridge to Data 🏗️
slides.content:
# Models = Database Tables

In Django, a **model** is a Python class that represents a single database table. Each **attribute** of the class becomes a **database column**.

Think of it like a blueprint:
- You define what kind of data you want to store (e.g., `title`, `author`, `published_date`).
- Django automatically creates the SQL to build the table and provides a Python API to interact with it.

> **Why models?** They keep your code database‑agnostic – you write Python, not SQL.

quizData.question: In Django, what does a model represent?

options.text: A single row in a database

quizData.explanation: A model class maps to a database table. Each instance of the model corresponds to a row in that table.

slides.title: Where Models Live 📁
slides.content:
Models are defined in the `models.py` file inside a Django app. For example, in an app called `blog`, you'd edit `blog/models.py`.

```
blog/
    models.py   <-- models go here
```

Django looks at all installed apps' `models.py` files to build the overall database schema.

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Always create models in the right app

Keep your app focused: if you're building a blog, put all blog‑related models (Post, Comment) in the `blog` app. Don't put them in `core` or `main` unless they are truly shared.
